title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1986 'Analysis situs (troisième mouture)' develops an axiomatics of 'ateliers'. An atelier A = (F, ≤, ≪) is a set F of 'figures' with two relations: ≤ (subfigure) and ≪ (roughly 'is interior to'). L ⊂ F denotes the point-like figures. The shadow omb(X) of a figure X is the set of points x ∈ L with x ≪ X. There is a canonical (co)morphism φ: F → Fig(L), F ↦ omb(F), into the 'set-theoretic' atelier of figures of L. Grothendieck wants to characterise the ateliers for which φ is an embedding onto a 'spacieux' sub-atelier, meaning closed under the gluings that exist in Fig(L). Page 54 states the proposition: (i) φ is an atelier embedding with spacious image, versus (ii) A is spacious in the absolute sense (axioms AtL1, AtL2, AtL3, AtCL(spac) of p.45) and distinct points are 'separated' (x ≠ y ⇒ x # y). Page 54 starts proving (i) ⇒ (ii) and checks AtL1: a non-empty figure has non-empty shadow interior.

This page continues (i) ⇒ (ii).

AtL2 (disjoint gluing). Let X, Y ∈ M have disjoint shadows, i.e. points of omb(X) and omb(Y) are pairwise distinct, equivalently pairwise separated (∥).
- Since omb(X) = |φ(X)| and likewise for Y, φ(X) and φ(Y) are disjoint figures of L.
- A fortiori they are gluable ('unionable') in Fig(L).
- By condition (i)(c), gluability reflects back, so X and Y are gluable in F.
- Moreover X ∩ Y = ∅, i.e. X and Y have no common subfigure. Otherwise a common subfigure Z would contain, by L1 (density of points), some point x ≪ Z. Then x would lie in omb(X) ∩ omb(Y), a contradiction.

AtCL(spac) (gluing along a common subfigure). Let X, Y ∈ M and L = X̃ ∩ Ỹ, their largest common subfigure. Suppose the points of omb(X) \ omb(L) and omb(Y) \ omb(L) are pairwise distinct, i.e. omb(X) ∩ omb(Y) = omb(L). Then |φ(X)| ∩ |φ(Y)| = |φ(L)|, so φ(L) is the maximal common subfigure of φ(X) and φ(Y). Hence φ(X) and φ(Y) are gluable along it in Fig(L), and by (c) X and Y are gluable.

Converse (ii) ⇒ (i), parts a) and c). Grothendieck first states Lemma 1. Let Λ ⊂ M be a dense part (an atlas) and φ_Λ: F → Fig(Λ), F ↦ mul omb_Λ(F), the multi-shadow relative to Λ. Then φ_Λ is 'strict': for every F, F' ↦ φ_Λ(F') is a bijection Ssfig(F) → Ssfig(φ_Λ(F)). Equivalently, F̃ → (φ_Λ(F))~ is an isomorphism of ordered sets.
- The margin notes that density of Λ is what makes φ_Λ strict.
- Page 56 reduces the lemma to the case Λ = M and then attacks c) via maximal common subfigures.

Overall purpose: a 'representation theorem' saying when an abstract combinatorial-topological structure of figures is faithfully realised by sets of points, with gluings (disjoint unions, unions along common subfigures) computed set-theoretically. This is part of Grothendieck's search for foundations of 'tame topology'.
errors: Slip: 'omb(x) ∩ omb(Y)' should read omb(X) ∩ omb(Y).

The step 'φ(X) ∥ φ(Y) ⇒ φ(X), φ(Y) gluable in Fig(L)' is taken for granted. It holds if Fig(L) is the set-theoretic atelier, where any union of figures is a figure, but this depends on the definition of Fig(L) in GF VI, which is not on this page.
AtCL step: deducing that φ(L) is the *maximal* common subfigure of φ(X), φ(Y) from |φ(X)| ∩ |φ(Y)| = |φ(L)| silently uses (i)(a), the bijection on subfigures. This is left implicit.
Lemma 1 is only stated here. The proof on p.56 is sketchy, and Grothendieck himself notes uncertainty about injectivity of φ.

ideas.what: Atelier (F, ≤, ≪): an abstract structure of figures with a subfigure relation and an interiority relation, axiomatising 'spaces' through their figures.
ideas.modern_name: Close to abstract stratified/tame structures, o-minimal-type axiomatics, and posets of cells or regular CW complexes; no exact modern counterpart.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984). o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s).
ideas.where_published: Only the general tame-topology aspiration appears in Esquisse d'un programme (§5); ateliers do not.

ideas.what: Shadow omb(X) and the canonical comorphism φ: F → Fig(L) to point-set figures; characterising when φ is an embedding with spacious image.
ideas.modern_name: Point-set realisation (spatialisation) theorem, analogous to the spatiality of locales or the geometric realisation of face posets.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogous results: Isbell and Joyal–Tierney for locales; Björner for regular CW posets.

ideas.what: Gluing axioms AtL2 (figures with disjoint shadows are disjoint and gluable) and AtCL (figures whose shadows meet exactly in the shadow of the maximal common subfigure are gluable along it), derived from the embedding condition.
ideas.modern_name: Closure under disjoint unions and pushouts along common subcomplexes (pasting axioms).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard for polyhedra and CW complexes.

ideas.what: Lemma 1: for a dense part Λ (atlas), the multi-shadow map is strict, i.e. an order isomorphism on posets of subfigures.
ideas.modern_name: Density, or a 'dense basis' property, giving a faithful representation.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatic tame topology via 'ateliers' (spacious and polyhedral) was never published or developed by others. The representation theorem characterising ateliers realisable by point sets with set-theoretic gluings is left half-proved: (ii) ⇒ (i) depends on Lemma 1, whose proof on p.56 is tentative.
missed.quote: (ii) ⟹ (i) a, c) Il faut prouver a) c) ... Lemme 1 ... Alors φ_Λ est stricte
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an intrinsic, figure-based alternative to o-minimal structures and to stratified-space foundations, which are of current interest in exodromy and stratified homotopy theory. Completing it could give a combinatorial axiomatics of tame spaces in the spirit of the Esquisse.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds routine verifications inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. The framework itself (ateliers) is largely unknown, but this page adds no striking result.
